title: Career roadmap · Professor
summary: Build an academic career in criminal law, criminology and forensic-law research through publications, teaching, funded research, supervision and institutional leadership.

facts.Timeline assumption: The student already holds a Ph.D., so the normal next step is a postdoctoral/research or faculty appointment rather than another master's. A Ph.D. alone does not guarantee appointment or promotion to professor; institutions apply their own recruitment and promotion rules.

horizons.question: What can I enter now?
horizons.output: Build a strong publication and teaching record and compete for faculty, research-fellow and academic appointments.

horizons.question: How should I specialise?
horizons.output: Establish a recognised academic niche such as criminal law, criminology, cybercrime, victimology, corrections, policing or forensic-law policy.

horizons.question: How should I evolve?
horizons.output: Lead funded research, supervise doctoral researchers, publish consistently and take on programme or departmental responsibilities.

horizons.question: How can I remain relevant?
horizons.output: Become an established scholar whose work connects criminal justice with empirical research, technology, forensic evidence and public policy.

rows.text: Prepare 3 complete course modules, reading lists and assessment rubrics
Complete one publishable doctrinal research article
Analyse one crime dataset and document methodology and limitations
Produce a research paper on forensic evidence, law and admissibility
Submit or publish a substantive peer-reviewed article
Draft one competitive research proposal with methodology, budget and outcomes
Present at least one research paper and archive the presentation
Maintain CV, ORCID, publications, teaching dossier and research proposals

blocks.text: Four-year honours variant

Not applicable to this Ph.D.-level starting point. If an earlier four-year UG honours pathway is being considered separately, the additional year should be used for an extended dissertation/research project and preparation for postgraduate study.

blocks.label: Evolve and stay relevant, 2035–2046
blocks.text: Keep developing both scholarly depth and research methods. A professor in this field benefits from understanding statistical analysis, administrative crime data, digital evidence and forensic science without blurring the distinction between legal scholarship and laboratory science.
Because the student already has a Ph.D., postdoctoral research, visiting appointments and research collaborations are generally more relevant than conventional student internships.

blocks.text: Ph.D./advanced research routes
The student already has a Ph.D., so the relevant advanced routes are:

The long-term objective is to become an independent academic authority rather than simply accumulate publications. A senior professor should have a coherent research agenda, a sustained publication record, successful supervision, competitive research funding, strong teaching, national/international collaborations and a recognised contribution to criminal-law or criminology scholarship.
